harrison-ch320:cb-inh.q: An 8-year-old boy has polyuria, growth delay and normal BP. Labs show K⁺ 2.6 mEq/L, HCO₃⁻ 32 mEq/L, high renin and aldosterone, high urinary calcium and nephrocalcinosis on ultrasound. The most likely defective transporter is:
o: NCC in the distal convoluted tubule
NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb
harrison-ch320:cb-inh.e: Bartter syndrome mimics loop diuretics: hypokalemic alkalosis with hypercalciuria. Gitelman (NCC) gives hypocalciuria and hypomagnesemia; ENaC gain (Liddle) causes hypertension with low renin.

harrison-ch320:cb-na.e: Disorders of Na⁺ concentration are disorders of water; ECF volume reflects total body Na⁺.

harrison-ch320:cb-na.q: ECF volume is determined mainly by:
harrison-ch320:cb-na.e: Regulated by RAAS, sympathetic activity, natriuretic peptides.

harrison-ch320:cb-na.q: A 70-year-old man with small cell lung cancer has confusion. He is euvolemic; serum Na⁺ is 122 mEq/L, serum osmolality 255 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 480 mOsm/kg and urine Na⁺ 50 mEq/L. His hyponatremia mainly reflects:
o: Renal salt wasting from low aldosterone
Sodium loss from the GI tract
harrison-ch320:cb-na.e: SIADH: ADH-driven water retention dilutes plasma Na⁺ in a euvolemic patient with inappropriately concentrated urine. Primary polydipsia would give maximally dilute urine (< 100 mOsm/kg).

harrison-ch321:aki-cause.q: The most common form of AKI is:
harrison-ch321:aki-cause.e: Harrison: prerenal azotemia is the most common form.

harrison-ch321:aki-cause.q: Why can NSAIDs precipitate AKI in a patient with heart failure?
o: They precipitate as crystals in tubules
They block angiotensin II efferent constriction
They cause direct toxic tubular necrosis
harrison-ch321:aki-cause.e: Autoregulation in low perfusion depends on afferent PG-mediated dilation and efferent Ang II constriction.
SCr rises in 1–2 days, peaks 3–5 days, recovers by ~7 days.

harrison-ch321:aki-cause.q: A 68-year-old smoker with refractory hypertension and an abdominal bruit is started on lisinopril. Within a week his creatinine rises from 1.3 to 2.5 mg/dL; urine sediment is bland. The mechanism of his AKI is:
harrison-ch321:aki-cause.e: With bilateral renal artery stenosis, GFR depends on angiotensin II constricting the efferent arteriole; an ACE inhibitor removes it and GFR falls. Afferent constriction is the NSAID/calcineurin mechanism.

harrison-ch321:aki-mx.q: Which is an indication for urgent dialysis in AKI?
harrison-ch321:aki-mx.e: Refractory volume overload, hyperkalemia, acidosis, some toxins, uremic complications (pericarditis, encephalopathy, bleeding).

harrison-ch321:aki-mx.q: AKI from scleroderma renal crisis should be treated with:

harrison-ch321:aki-mx.e: May need up to 10 L/day of fluid.

harrison-ch321:aki-mx.q: A 66-year-old man with oliguric AKI has K⁺ 7.1 mEq/L. ECG shows peaked T waves and a widened QRS. The first drug to give, and its effect, is:
o: IV insulin: shifts K⁺ into the cells
Patiromer: binds K⁺ in the colon
harrison-ch321:aki-mx.e: With ECG changes, IV calcium is given first to stabilize the myocardium within minutes; it does not lower K⁺. Insulin with glucose follows to shift K⁺ intracellularly.

harrison-ch322:ckd-stage.q: eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73m² with ACR 150 mg/g is classified as:
In the KDIGO heat map, risk of CKD progression increases with:
o: Falling GFR only; albuminuria adds no risk
Rising albuminuria only; GFR adds no risk
harrison-ch322:ckd-stage.e: Both axes independently increase mortality, CV death and progression.

harrison-ch322:ckd-stage.q: A 60-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has an eGFR of 52 mL/min/1.73 m² on two measurements 4 months apart and a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 420 mg/g. Her CKD category is:
harrison-ch322:ckd-stage.e: eGFR 45–59 = G3a; ACR > 300 mg/g = A3 (severely increased). A2 is 30–300 mg/g.

harrison-ch322:ckd-lyte.q: Hyperkalemia out of proportion to GFR in a diabetic with CKD suggests:
harrison-ch322:ckd-lyte.e: Type 4 RTA pattern in diabetes, obstruction, sickle cell nephropathy.

harrison-ch322:ckd-lyte.q: Metabolic acidosis in early CKD is usually non–anion gap because:
harrison-ch322:ckd-lyte.e: Reduced ammoniagenesis limits acid excretion; anion-gap acidosis appears as GFR falls further.

harrison-ch322:ckd-lyte.q: A 62-year-old man with diabetic CKD (eGFR 45) has K⁺ 5.9 mEq/L and a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. Plasma renin and aldosterone are both low, and urine pH is 5.2. The most likely disorder is:
harrison-ch322:ckd-lyte.e: Hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism in diabetic CKD causes type 4 RTA: hyperkalemia with NAGMA and preserved ability to acidify urine. Type 1 RTA has urine pH > 5.5 and usually hypokalemia.

harrison-ch322:ckd-slow.q: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce intraglomerular pressure by:
harrison-ch322:ckd-slow.e: More NaCl reaches the macula densa → tubuloglomerular feedback → afferent vasoconstriction.

harrison-ch322:ckd-slow.q: Combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB in CKD:
harrison-ch322:ckd-slow.e: Dual RAS blockade increases harm (more AKI and cardiac events).

harrison-ch322:ckd-slow.q: Target BP in proteinuric CKD per Harrison:
A 56-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73 m² and ACR 600 mg/g despite maximal-dose losartan; BP is 128/78 mm Hg. The best addition to slow CKD progression is:
harrison-ch322:ckd-slow.e: SGLT2 inhibitors restore tubuloglomerular feedback (afferent constriction), lowering intraglomerular pressure and slowing CKD. Adding an ACE inhibitor to an ARB raises hyperkalemia and AKI risk without benefit.

harrison-ch323:hd.q: The principal mechanism of solute removal in hemodialysis is:
harrison-ch323:hd.e: Diffusion across a semipermeable membrane, down concentration gradients; ultrafiltration removes water.

harrison-ch323:hd.q: The vascular access with the longest patency and lowest infection rate:
The leading cause of ESKD in the United States:
harrison-ch323:hd.e: Diabetes accounts for ~45% of new ESKD cases (Harrison Ch 323).

harrison-ch323:hd.q: A 58-year-old man on thrice-weekly hemodialysis gains 3 kg of fluid between sessions. Removal of this excess fluid during treatment occurs mainly by:
harrison-ch323:hd.e: Fluid is removed by ultrafiltration, driven by a transmembrane hydrostatic pressure gradient; solutes like urea are removed by diffusion. Dextrose-driven osmotic ultrafiltration is how peritoneal dialysis removes fluid.

harrison-ch323:hdcx.q: The most common acute complication of hemodialysis:
harrison-ch323:hdcx.e: Especially in diabetics; manage by stopping UF and giving saline.

harrison-ch323:hdcx.q: Ultrafiltration rates above which value are associated with cardiovascular death?
A 19-year-old with newly diagnosed ESKD and BUN 180 mg/dL develops headache, vomiting and a seizure near the end of his first, long hemodialysis session. The mechanism is:
o: Air embolism through the venous line
Cerebral edema from rapid urea removal
harrison-ch323:hdcx.e: Dialysis disequilibrium: rapid lowering of plasma urea leaves brain osmolality higher, drawing water into the brain. It is prevented by short, gentle initial sessions.

harrison-ch323:pd.q: Peritonitis in a PD patient is defined by effluent WBC ≥100/mm³ with at least:
harrison-ch323:pd.e: Lower thresholds than SBP because of dextrose.

harrison-ch323:pd.q: Icodextrin in PD is used for:
harrison-ch323:pd.e: Used as last fill in CCPD or longest dwell in CAPD.

harrison-ch323:pd.q: A 52-year-old woman on peritoneal dialysis has abdominal pain and cloudy effluent. Effluent WBC count is 450/mm³ with 85% neutrophils; there is no exit-site discharge. The most likely organism is:
harrison-ch323:pd.e: PD peritonitis is most often from skin flora (coagulase-negative staphylococci) introduced at exchanges. Gram-negative or fungal peritonitis is less common and suggests bowel source or prior antibiotics.

harrison-ch324:ivn.q: An AV fistula that is hyperpulsatile and does not soften in diastole suggests:
harrison-ch324:ivn.e: Outflow stenosis increases pulsatility; inflow stenosis gives a weak 'empty' access.

harrison-ch324:ivn.q: An access with excessively high flow can be treated by:
harrison-ch324:ivn.e: Banding creates a controlled inflow stenosis.

harrison-ch324:ivn.q: A 60-year-old man on hemodialysis via a left arm AV fistula has progressive swelling of the entire left arm, with dilated veins over the chest wall. Fistula pressures are high during dialysis. The most likely cause is:
harrison-ch324:ivn.e: Whole-arm edema with chest wall collaterals means venous outflow is blocked centrally, often after prior central catheters. Steal causes hand pain and pallor, not swelling.

harrison-ch325:tx-imm.e: Prevented by ABO matching and crossmatch.

harrison-ch325:tx-imm.q: C4d staining in peritubular capillaries indicates:
harrison-ch325:tx-imm.e: Footprint of complement activation by donor-specific antibodies.

harrison-ch325:tx-imm.q: CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cells respond primarily to donor:
harrison-ch325:tx-imm.e: CD4 → class II; CD8 → class I.

harrison-ch325:tx-imm.q: A 45-year-old man has a rising creatinine 3 months after a deceased-donor kidney transplant. Biopsy shows interstitial lymphocytes invading tubular epithelium (tubulitis); C4d staining is negative and donor-specific antibodies are absent. The diagnosis is:
harrison-ch325:tx-imm.e: Tubulitis with interstitial lymphocytes and no C4d/DSA is acute cellular rejection, driven by T cells recognizing donor HLA. C4d-positive capillaritis indicates antibody-mediated rejection.

harrison-ch325:tx-drug.q: Gingival hyperplasia and hirsutism are typical of:

o: Blocking the IL-2 receptor α chain
harrison-ch325:tx-drug.e: Costimulation blockade: binds CD80/CD86 on APCs, preventing CD28 costimulation.

harrison-ch325:tx-drug.q: A 52-year-old woman on a three-drug regimen after kidney transplant develops tremor, new-onset diabetes, hyperkalemia and hypertension. Trough level of one drug is high. That drug acts by:
o: Blocking CD80/86 binding to T-cell CD28
harrison-ch325:tx-drug.e: Tremor, diabetes, hyperkalemia and hypertension are classic tacrolimus toxicity; it binds FKBP-12 and inhibits calcineurin, blocking IL-2 gene transcription. mTOR inhibitors act downstream of the IL-2 receptor.

harrison-ch325:tx-inf.q: Cytomegalovirus and Pneumocystis infections after kidney transplant peak at:
The most common malignancies after kidney transplantation are:
Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease is most often associated with:

Ten weeks after a kidney transplant, a 50-year-old man (donor CMV-positive, recipient CMV-negative) has fever, leukopenia and elevated transaminases. Blood PCR shows a high viral load. The best treatment is:
harrison-ch325:tx-inf.e: CMV disease peaks 1–6 months after transplant, especially D+/R−; ganciclovir or valganciclovir is the treatment. Acyclovir has poor CMV activity.

harrison-ch326:gd-prot.q: Microalbuminuria is defined as albumin excretion of:
In normal urine, albumin accounts for what fraction of total urinary protein?
harrison-ch326:gd-prot.e: Normal urine (total protein < 150 mg/day) is mostly tubular uromodulin (Tamm–Horsfall) and filtered low-molecular-weight proteins; albumin is a minority (~20–60%). In glomerular proteinuria albumin becomes the dominant protein.

harrison-ch326:gd-prot.q: A 45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes has a urine dipstick negative for protein, but a spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 120 mg/g on two occasions. This finding is classified as:
harrison-ch326:gd-prot.e: ACR 30–300 mg/g (formerly microalbuminuria) is moderately increased albuminuria (A2), often below dipstick sensitivity. It is the earliest clinical sign of diabetic kidney disease.

harrison-ch326:gd-pat.e: With anti-GBM disease, thin BM disease, nail-patella.

harrison-ch326:gd-pat.q: A 65-year-old man with a prosthetic valve has 4 weeks of fever; blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. He develops hematuria with RBC casts, low C3 and creatinine 2.3 mg/dL. The kidney lesion is most likely:
harrison-ch326:gd-pat.e: Endocarditis causes an infection-associated nephritic syndrome with low complement from circulating immune complexes. Anti-GBM disease has normal complement and linear IgG.

harrison-ch326:gd-tx.q: First-line treatment of minimal change disease:
harrison-ch326:gd-tx.e: Steroid; other agents for relapses or resistance.

harrison-ch326:gd-tx.q: Pulmonary hemorrhage in anti-GBM disease responds to:

harrison-ch326:gd-tx.e: Reduces proteinuria in IgAN at risk of progression.

harrison-ch326:gd-tx.q: A 50-year-old man has chronic sinusitis, lung nodules, RBC casts and creatinine 3.2 mg/dL. PR3-ANCA is positive and biopsy shows pauci-immune crescentic GN. The most appropriate induction therapy is:
harrison-ch326:gd-tx.e: ANCA-associated GN is induced with glucocorticoids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide. Budesonide is for IgA nephropathy and eculizumab for atypical HUS.

harrison-ch327:pkd-ad.q: ADPKD is caused by mutations in PKD1 in about what proportion of cases?
The most common extrarenal manifestation of ADPKD:
harrison-ch327:pkd-ad.e: Liver cysts; aneurysms 4–5× more frequent than general population.
V2 antagonist: lowers cAMP, which drives cyst growth.

harrison-ch327:pkd-ad.q: A 38-year-old woman with ADPKD has eGFR 70 mL/min/1.73 m² and rapidly enlarging kidneys on MRI. She starts a drug that slows cyst growth by lowering cAMP in collecting duct cells. Which monitoring is most important?
harrison-ch327:pkd-ad.e: Tolvaptan (V2 antagonist) can cause serious liver injury, so liver enzymes are checked regularly; its other main effect is aquaresis with thirst and polyuria.

harrison-ch327:pkd-ar.q: ARPKD is caused by mutations in:
The liver lesion in ARPKD is:

A newborn has respiratory distress, flattened facies and massively enlarged echogenic kidneys; pregnancy was complicated by oligohydramnios and both parents are healthy. The renal cysts in this disorder arise mainly from the:
harrison-ch327:pkd-ar.e: ARPKD (PKHD1) causes radially arranged fusiform dilation of collecting ducts throughout the cortex and medulla; survivors develop congenital hepatic fibrosis.

harrison-ch327:pkd-oth.q: Renal cysts with multifocal clear cell RCC, cerebellar hemangioblastoma and pheochromocytoma:
CKD with gout and few cysts in a family with UMOD mutation:

A 12-year-old girl has polyuria, polydipsia, growth failure and anemia; creatinine is 2.6 mg/dL with bland urine. Ultrasound shows normal-sized echogenic kidneys with small corticomedullary cysts, and she has retinal degeneration. The likely diagnosis is:
harrison-ch327:pkd-oth.e: Nephronophthisis is an autosomal recessive ciliopathy with a salt-wasting, concentrating defect, small corticomedullary cysts and ESKD in childhood (Senior–Løken with retinal disease). Medullary sponge kidney is benign with normal function.

harrison-ch328:tin-ain.q: The classic triad of drug-induced AIN (fever, rash, eosinophilia) is:
o: The exception rather than the rule
harrison-ch328:tin-ain.e: Harrison: most patients lack the full triad.

harrison-ch328:tin-ain.q: First step in suspected drug-induced AIN:
harrison-ch328:tin-ain.e: Then steroids if no improvement in ~1 week or rapid progression.

harrison-ch328:tin-ain.q: A 68-year-old woman develops AKI 3 weeks after starting nafcillin. Biopsy shows interstitial edema with lymphocytes and eosinophils. The drug was stopped, but after 7 days her creatinine is still rising. The next best step is:
harrison-ch328:tin-ain.e: If biopsy-proven drug-induced AIN does not improve after withdrawal, glucocorticoids may hasten recovery. Re-exposure is contraindicated, and there is no dialysis indication.

harrison-ch328:tin-imm.q: Sjögren syndrome renal involvement typically causes:
harrison-ch328:tin-imm.e: Most common renal manifestation; may also cause nephrogenic DI.

harrison-ch328:tin-imm.q: TIN with uveitis (TINU) is treated with:
harrison-ch328:tin-imm.e: Absolute indication for steroids in adults.

harrison-ch328:tin-imm.q: A 40-year-old woman has bilateral hilar adenopathy, calcium 11.8 mg/dL and creatinine 2.2 mg/dL with sterile pyuria. A kidney biopsy would most likely show:
harrison-ch328:tin-imm.e: Sarcoidosis causes granulomatous interstitial nephritis and hypercalcemia from macrophage 1α-hydroxylase. Lymphocytic TIN without granulomas is typical of Sjögren syndrome.

harrison-ch328:tin-chronic.q: Herbal weight-loss preparations causing interstitial fibrosis and urothelial carcinoma contain:
harrison-ch328:tin-chronic.e: Aristolochic acid nephropathy (Chinese herbal / Balkan nephropathy).

harrison-ch328:tin-chronic.q: Chronic lithium therapy most characteristically causes:
Which is NOT a major cause of papillary necrosis?

A 50-year-old man with bipolar disorder has taken lithium at therapeutic levels for 20 years. He passes 5 L of urine daily; urine osmolality is 150 mOsm/kg and does not rise after desmopressin. The mechanism is:
o: Deficient ADH release from the pituitary
harrison-ch328:tin-chronic.e: Lithium enters principal cells via ENaC and down-regulates AQP2, causing nephrogenic DI. Central DI would respond to desmopressin.

harrison-ch329:tma-types.q: TTP is defined by MAHA with ADAMTS13 activity below:

A 35-year-old woman has fever, confusion and petechiae. Hemoglobin is 7.8 g/dL with schistocytes, platelets 18,000/µL, LDH high and creatinine 1.6 mg/dL. ADAMTS13 activity is < 5%. The most appropriate treatment is:
harrison-ch329:tma-types.e: Acquired TTP (anti-ADAMTS13) is treated with urgent plasma exchange plus glucocorticoids (± caplacizumab). Eculizumab is for complement-mediated (atypical) HUS.

harrison-ch329:tma-ssc.e: AKI with abrupt hypertension and a bland sediment. Treat with ACE inhibitors.

harrison-ch329:tma-ssc.q: Scleroderma renal crisis occurs in what proportion of diffuse systemic sclerosis?

A 45-year-old woman with rapidly progressive diffuse skin thickening, recently started on high-dose prednisone, has BP 210/120 mm Hg, schistocytes and rising creatinine. The autoantibody most associated with this complication is:
harrison-ch329:tma-ssc.e: Scleroderma renal crisis is associated with early diffuse disease, anti-RNA polymerase III and high-dose glucocorticoids. Anticentromere marks limited disease with low renal-crisis risk.

harrison-ch330:st-type.q: Uric acid stones form when urine pH is consistently:
Staghorn calculi in a patient with recurrent Proteus UTIs are composed of:
harrison-ch330:st-type.e: Struvite = magnesium ammonium phosphate. Urease raises urine pH >8.

harrison-ch330:st-type.q: A 55-year-old man with gout has renal colic. The stone is not visible on plain x-ray but is seen on CT; urine pH is 5.0 on repeated samples. The best long-term therapy to dissolve and prevent these stones is:
harrison-ch330:st-type.e: Radiolucent stones in persistently acidic urine are uric acid; alkalinizing urine with potassium citrate dissolves and prevents them. Thiazides target hypercalciuric calcium stones.

harrison-ch330:st-risk.q: Higher dietary calcium intake is associated with:
o: Lower risk of calcium oxalate stones
Higher risk of calcium oxalate stones
harrison-ch330:st-risk.e: Dietary calcium binds oxalate in the gut; supplements may differ.

harrison-ch330:st-risk.q: Recommended urine volume for stone prevention:

A 40-year-old man with recurrent calcium oxalate stones follows a strict low-calcium diet. His 24-hour urine shows volume 1.1 L, high oxalate and normal calcium. The most appropriate dietary advice is:
harrison-ch330:st-risk.e: Dietary calcium binds oxalate in the gut, so a low-calcium diet raises oxalate absorption and stone risk; also aim for ≥ 2 L/day urine. Vitamin C is metabolized to oxalate.

harrison-ch330:st-mx.q: The imaging of choice for suspected renal colic:
In cystinuria, urine is alkalinized with potassium citrate rather than sodium salts because:
A drug that can increase spontaneous passage of a ureteral stone:
A 50-year-old woman has left flank pain, fever of 39.4 °C and BP 88/56 mm Hg. CT shows an 8-mm obstructing proximal ureteral stone with hydronephrosis. After starting antibiotics, the next step is:
harrison-ch330:st-mx.e: An infected obstructed kidney is a urologic emergency requiring prompt decompression; definitive stone treatment is deferred. Medical expulsive therapy is only for uncomplicated small stones.

harrison-ch331:uo-cause.q: The most common cause of bilateral hydronephrosis in boys:
Obstruction above the bladder typically produces:
harrison-ch331:uo-cause.e: Unilateral hydroureter/hydronephrosis. Lesions at or below the bladder cause bilateral involvement.

harrison-ch331:uo-cause.q: A 48-year-old woman has postcoital and intermenstrual bleeding, pelvic pain and creatinine 3.1 mg/dL. Ultrasound shows bilateral hydronephrosis with a normal bladder. The most likely cause of obstruction is:
harrison-ch331:uo-cause.e: Locally advanced cervical cancer invades the parametrium and compresses both ureters, a classic cause of bilateral hydronephrosis in women. Bilateral simultaneous stones are rare.

harrison-ch331:uo-phys.q: Partial bilateral urinary obstruction often causes:
harrison-ch331:uo-phys.e: Hyperkalemic distal RTA with salt wasting, plus acquired nephrogenic DI.

harrison-ch331:uo-phys.q: Acute partial bilateral obstruction can mimic:
harrison-ch331:uo-phys.e: High BUN/Cr, concentrated urine, Na retention.

harrison-ch331:uo-phys.q: A 72-year-old man with prostatic enlargement reports 3.5 L/day of urine and nocturia; ultrasound shows bilateral hydronephrosis. Urine osmolality is 240 mOsm/kg and does not rise after desmopressin. The polyuria is best explained by:
harrison-ch331:uo-phys.e: Partial obstruction damages tubules and down-regulates AQP2, causing an acquired nephrogenic DI-like concentrating defect. Central DI would respond to desmopressin.

harrison-ch331:uo-dx.q: Hydronephrosis may be absent on ultrasound despite obstruction when:
o: The bladder is distended and full
harrison-ch331:uo-dx.e: Very early obstruction (<48 h) or retroperitoneal fibrosis; also volume contraction, staghorn calculi, infiltrative disease.

harrison-ch331:uo-dx.q: After how long of complete obstruction is recovery of GFR unlikely?
harrison-ch331:uo-dx.e: Partial recovery after 1–2 weeks; unlikely after 8 weeks.

harrison-ch331:uo-dx.q: Postobstructive diuresis typically follows relief of:
harrison-ch331:uo-dx.e: Hypotonic urine rich in Na, K, PO₄, Mg.

harrison-ch331:uo-dx.q: A 76-year-old man has suprapubic pain and has not voided for 18 hours. The bladder is palpable to the umbilicus, creatinine is 3.8 mg/dL and ultrasound shows bilateral hydronephrosis. The best initial step is:
harrison-ch331:uo-dx.e: Bladder outlet obstruction is relieved first with a urethral (or suprapubic) catheter; watch for postobstructive diuresis afterward. Nephrostomies are for obstruction above the bladder.

title.th: เด็กหน้าบวมตอนเช้า

stem.th: เด็กชาย 5 ปี ตาบวมตอนตื่นนอนมา 1 สัปดาห์ ตอนนี้ขาบวมด้วย ไม่มีไข้ ความดันปกติ
stem.en: A 5-year-old boy has had puffy eyes on waking for a week, now with leg swelling. No fever, normal BP.

info.th: UA: protein 4+, ไม่มีเม็ดเลือดแดง · albumin 1.8 g/dL · cholesterol สูง
info.en: UA: protein 4+, no RBCs · albumin 1.8 g/dL · high cholesterol

steps.e: Heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema and hyperlipidemia without hematuria = nephrotic syndrome.

steps.q: Most likely cause in this age group:
steps.e: Minimal change disease is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children.

info.th: ทำ renal biopsy: LM ปกติ
info.en: Renal biopsy: light microscopy is normal

steps.e: MCD: diffuse foot-process effacement of podocytes; LM and IF are normal.

steps.q: Which part of the filtration barrier is chiefly disrupted?
steps.e: Loss of the podocyte slit diaphragm/polyanion barrier lets albumin leak (selective proteinuria).
MCD responds well to corticosteroids.

title.th: ปวดเอวร้าวลงขาหนีบ

stem.th: ชาย 35 ปี ปวดเอวขวาบิดเป็นพักๆ ร้าวลงขาหนีบ กระสับกระส่าย คลื่นไส้
stem.en: A 35-year-old man has colicky right flank pain radiating to the groin, restless and nauseated.

steps.e: Non-contrast CT shows stone size, site and obstruction; ultrasound is preferred in pregnancy.

info.th: CT: นิ่ว 5 mm ค้างที่ท่อไตส่วนปลายสุด
info.en: CT: 5 mm stone at the distal end of the ureter

steps.q: The narrowest point where stones commonly lodge here is the:
steps.e: Three constrictions: PUJ, pelvic brim (iliac vessels), and the UVJ, the narrowest.
Calcium oxalate stones are the most common type.

steps.q: Which drug reduces calcium excretion to prevent recurrence?
steps.e: Thiazides increase distal Ca²⁺ reabsorption; loop diuretics increase calcium loss.

title.th: ปัสสาวะน้อยหลังช็อก

stem.th: หญิง 68 ปี หลังผ่าตัดลำไส้มีภาวะช็อกจากติดเชื้อ 6 ชม. วันต่อมาปัสสาวะออกน้อย creatinine ขึ้นจาก 0.9 เป็น 3.1
stem.en: A 68-year-old woman had 6 hours of septic shock after bowel surgery. Next day she is oliguric; creatinine rose from 0.9 to 3.1.

info.th: UA: muddy brown granular casts · FeNa 3%
info.en: UA: muddy brown granular casts · FENa 3%

steps.e: Muddy brown casts and FENa > 2% indicate intrinsic tubular injury (ATN).

steps.q: Which segments are most vulnerable to ischemia?
o: Papillary collecting ducts and thin limbs in the inner medulla
Proximal straight tubule and TAL in the outer medulla
steps.e: The pars recta and TAL have high O₂ demand in a poorly perfused outer medulla.

info.en: K⁺ 6.8 mEq/L · ECG shows peaked T waves

steps.e: Calcium stabilizes the myocardium first; then shift K⁺ (insulin/glucose) and remove it.

steps.q: The granular casts are made of a matrix protein secreted by the:
steps.e: Casts form on a Tamm-Horsfall (uromodulin) matrix secreted by the TAL.

title.th: ไข้สูงปวดเอว

stem.th: หญิง 24 ปี ไข้ 39.2°C หนาวสั่น ปวดเอวซ้าย เคาะเจ็บ มีปัสสาวะแสบขัดมา 3 วัน
stem.en: A 24-year-old woman has fever 39.2°C, rigors and left flank pain with CVA tenderness after 3 days of dysuria.

info.th: UA: WBC มาก มี WBC casts, nitrite +
info.en: UA: many WBCs, WBC casts, nitrite positive

steps.q: Which finding localizes infection to the kidney rather than the bladder?
steps.e: Casts form in tubules, so WBC casts indicate renal parenchymal involvement.
Most pyelonephritis is ascending; the short female urethra favors this.

info.th: ถ้าดูเนื้อไตใต้กล้อง
info.en: If the kidney were examined histologically

o: Neutrophils in collecting ducts and interstitium
steps.e: Acute pyelonephritis: neutrophils fill tubules (especially collecting ducts) and interstitium.
Uropathogenic E. coli causes most community UTIs.

title.th: เบาหวานสิบห้าปี

stem.th: ชาย 55 ปี เบาหวานชนิดที่ 2 มา 15 ปี คุมไม่ดี ตรวจสุขภาพประจำปี
stem.en: A 55-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes for 15 years comes for a check-up.

steps.q: The earliest structural change in diabetic kidney disease is:
steps.e: GBM thickening and mesangial expansion come first; nodules appear later.
Nodular glomerulosclerosis = Kimmelstiel–Wilson lesions.

steps.q: Which drug slows progression by lowering intraglomerular pressure?
steps.e: ACE inhibitors/ARBs dilate the efferent arteriole, lowering glomerular pressure and proteinuria.

steps.q: Hyaline arteriolosclerosis in diabetes classically affects:
steps.e: Diabetes involves both arterioles; hypertension mainly the afferent.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ฉี่สีโค้ก

renal.case: A 7-year-old boy is brought in with puffy eyes and dark, cola-colored urine. Three weeks ago he had crusted, honey-colored skin sores on his legs. BP is 138/90 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows hematuria and protein 1+.

qs.q: What is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Nephritic syndrome 2–4 weeks after group A strep skin or throat infection. IgA nephropathy follows a URI within days.

qs.q: Which urine sediment finding best supports this?

o: High C3 with normal ASO titers
Low C3 and high ASO/anti-DNase B
qs.e: Immune complexes activate complement; anti-DNase B is more reliable after skin infection.

qs.q: Electron microscopy of a biopsy would show:
qs.e: Light microscopy: hypercellular glomeruli; IF: granular 'starry sky' IgG, IgM, C3.

qs.q: His hypertension and edema are mainly due to:
o: Na⁺ and water retention from ↓ GFR
qs.e: Nephritic syndrome reduces filtration → volume expansion. Edema in nephrotic syndrome is driven by hypoalbuminemia.

o: Recurrent gross hematuria with every URI
Rapid progression to ESRD in most children
qs.e: Children usually recover; adults more often develop RPGN or CKD.
